answer: Each agent identity must be minted through a proof-of-inference challenge where the newcomer burns scarce GPU cycles on a uniquely seeded task; the resulting lagoon of verified compute logs anchors identity to real resource expenditure. Attestations then propagate through a plume of cross-checks among established peers, and once an identity settles into the reef of long-lived reputation, every new sybil must independently reproduce that full inference cost rather than cloning credentials, making mass identity creation linearly expensive in the scarcest commodity agents have.
